title: Sovereign Citizens: Pseudolaw & Disorder
summary: Long comedic debunk tracing sovereign-citizen and freeman pseudolaw from the Posse Comitatus to Canada, the UK, Ireland, Germany and Australasia, its word magic, violence and grifts.

assertions.quote: Robert Menard's adaptation of the sovcit grift to a commonwealth country made it oven ready for its journey across the Atlantic Ocean.

verdicts.note: Researchers and court rulings (e.g. Meads v Meads) document the same pseudolegal arguments recast for Canada, the UK, Australia, New Zealand and Germany.

assertions.quote: The Posse Comitatus were a group of manchildren who came together in the seventies because they had a hatred of the government

verdicts.note: Historians and the SPLC/ADL trace the modern movement to William Potter Gale's Posse Comitatus and 1970s-80s tax protesters.

assertions.quote: many gurus realised that paramilitaristic racism was profitable and sold seminars, cassette box sets and guide books

verdicts.note: Prosecutions and court rulings repeatedly describe gurus charging for seminars, templates and services that do not work.

assertions.quote: sovcits were considered the highest potential threat by law enforcement out of all extremist groups

verdicts.note: There are documented killings of officers and law-enforcement surveys rank the threat highly, but adherents account for a small share of attacks on police and most never turn violent.

assertions.quote: They would typically target them with property liens as this bypasses the judicial system.

verdicts.note: Bogus liens against officials ('paper terrorism') are well documented and led many states to pass laws against them.

assertions.quote: They use economic crises to reel in new recruits

verdicts.note: Recruitment surges are documented around the 1980s farm crisis, 2008 foreclosures and COVID, though growth also tracks the internet and other factors.

assertions.quote: if a new statutory law disagrees with a common law, then that new codified statutory law takes precedent.

verdicts.note: In common-law countries legislation overrides common law and nobody can opt out of statutes; courts reject Magna Carta and natural-law exemptions.

assertions.quote: no record of a sovereign citizen argument being used in court or screamed at a police officer

verdicts.note: US and Commonwealth courts consistently dismiss these arguments, often calling them frivolous; no case has accepted the theories on their merits.

assertions.quote: Mr. Meads is Mr. Meads in all physical or imaginary aspects.

verdicts.note: No such entity exists; courts uniformly hold that the person and the name, in any capitalisation, are the same legal person.

assertions.quote: They believe that they are exempt from all laws, and they use this to claim land that they don't own

verdicts.note: The 1786 treaty is an ordinary peace-and-trade treaty; courts reject Moorish immunity claims and convict defendants who make them.

assertions.quote: the federal US government has been a private corporation since sometime during the American Civil War, or 1871

verdicts.note: The 1871 Act created a municipal government for DC, later repealed; it did not incorporate the United States, and courts reject the argument.

assertions.quote: sometimes they'll fraudulently deed empty homes and just move in.

verdicts.note: Numerous prosecutions involve sovereign or Moorish adherents filing bogus deeds and squatting in vacant or listed homes.
TSILC/USN members squatted illegally in Alberta and their leader tried to seize his landlady's rental property as an 'embassy'; real but no fake deeds are described and only one group.
